datasets.title: Who makes what: store-brand answers (Kirkland Signature)
datasets.what: Every store-brand product we can answer from a public record, one row per company the record names: the product, the company, what the record says it did (made, bottled, imported, recalled), the stamp, the dates and lots it covers, the words to look for on the label, and links to the records.
datasets.limits: Each row covers only its own dates, lots and region. A label approval names the bottler or importer, not always the distiller; a recall names the recalling firm, usually but not always the maker.
datasets.use: Powers the Kirkland Signature hub and its answer pages.
datasets.refresh: Whenever a claim is added or re-checked; every claim is re-checked within 6 months
datasets.rights: Quoted words belong to their publishers; most records are US government work. CC BY covers our rows.

datasets.title: Which store labels each company is on record for
datasets.what: One row per link between a company and a brand or retailer: a claim on our answer pages, a registration on North Dakota’s pet food register filed in the company’s care, a store name printed in the company’s FDA recalls, or a brand listed under the company’s API engine oil license. Each row says how many records back it, the dates they cover, and links the record.
datasets.limits: A register row shows the company is the registered contact for those products, not that it made each one. A recall row shows the store name was printed in the recall’s product text; it doesn’t prove a current supply deal. Rows cover only their own dates. An API license row shows the company answers to API for that brand’s oils, not which plant blended them or who owns the brand.

datasets.title: Tire age guidance from tire makers, carmakers and agencies
datasets.what: What each tire maker, carmaker and safety agency says about replacing tires by age, in a row per maker: the age, what it’s counted from, whether it covers the spare, and the document it comes from.
datasets.limits: Each row speaks only for the maker’s own tires, or for the vehicle model and year named. It is advice, not law, except the UK row, which describes a legal ban on tires over 10 years old for some heavy vehicles.
datasets.use: Powers the Tire age checker and its two tables.
datasets.refresh: Re-read in a browser every year, and whenever a maker changes its advice
datasets.rights: Quoted words in the source columns belong to their publishers; we quote them so you can check each row. CC BY covers our rows and wording.

preview.also: Says some vehicle and tire makers recommend replacing tires 6 to 10 years old regardless of tread, that you can't spot aging by looking, and that spares age because they're seldom replaced.
preview.source_titles: NHTSA, Tires: aging | NHTSA, Tires: what can I do? | NHTSA, Tires: be aware of your spare | NHTSA, Tires: am I at risk? | NHTSA, Tires: what speeds aging | NHTSA, Tires: should I replace my tires? | NHTSA, Tires: full-size spares
preview.quotes: As tires age, they are more prone to failure. Some vehicle and tire manufacturers recommend replacing tires that are six to 10 years old, regardless of treadwear. | You cannot detect tire aging simply by looking at your tires. | Spare tires on all vehicles are prone to aging because they seldom get replaced. | Most of us drive our vehicles enough that the tires’ treads wear out, and we replace our tires before aging becomes an issue. | In addition to infrequent use, exposure to sunlight and warmer climate, poor storage and poor maintenance also contribute to tire aging. | You should stop using tires for several reasons, including if a tire’s tread is worn down to a minimum depth using the penny test, signs of physical damage (cuts, cracks, bulges, etc.), or signs of irregular wear or other damage due to underinflation or overloading. | NHTSA recommends that if your vehicle comes equipped with a full-size spare tire, that it not be used as a replacement for worn tires, except in emergencies such as replacing a flat tire.

datasets.title: Evidence records: every quote behind our answers

datasets.limits: A record shows what a document said when we read it. Documents change; the fingerprint lets you check whether the one you have is the same.
datasets.use: Every quote and citation on the site comes from these records.
datasets.refresh: Whenever we read or re-read a document
datasets.rights: Quotes belong to their publishers and are short so you can check our work. CC BY covers our records: titles, notes, dates and fingerprints.

datasets.title: Craftsman model numbers and the companies government records name for them
datasets.what: One row per record that ties a Craftsman model number to a company: battery-charger filings on California's appliance register (MAEDbS), EPA small-engine certificates from its 1997-2010 archive that list Craftsman or Sears models, and CPSC recalls that mention Craftsman. Each row gives the company, its role in the record, the year, the model numbers and, for Sears-era models, the three-digit Sears source code.
datasets.limits: A record names a company for the models it lists, not for every Craftsman product, and isn't a look at any unit. A charger filing names the company that filed it, which is often Stanley Black & Decker itself; an engine certificate names the engine's maker of record, not who assembled the tool; a recall names the manufacturer, importer or distributor as the CPSC gives them. Sellers (Sears, Kmart, Orchard Supply, Ace) are left out of the company column.
datasets.use: Powers the Craftsman model number lookup and its Sears code decoder.
datasets.refresh: Monthly, from California's register, CPSC recalls and Stanley Black & Decker's newest SEC report

datasets.title: Trader Joe's wine, beer and spirits label approvals (TTB)
datasets.what: Every label approval in TTB's public COLA registry with a brand name starting "Trader Joe", for the 15 years the registry's search allows: the approval number, the kind of drink, TTB's class, the company that holds the approval (box 8 of the form), the trade name the form says goes on the bottle, origin, date and status, with a link to each form.
datasets.limits: An approval shows which company applied for a label and got it approved, not that the label is on shelves now, and not which of several holders filled the bottle in front of you. One approval covers one label design, so a new vintage or size adds a row; it is not a count of bottles. Six approvals whose form gave no applicant are left out. "holder" groups spellings and related Sazerac companies; "applicant" is as filed.
datasets.use: Powers the wine, beer and spirits section of the Trader Joe's page.
datasets.refresh: Read in full from TTB's registry when the page is re-checked (next May 2027)
